title: Investment Banking Roles and Teams
excerpt: Compare investment banking roles and teams, see where operations fits in the transaction lifecycle, and identify practical skills for entry-level work.

body.text: Investment banking roles are organised differently across firms, products and markets. A useful team map separates client or market activity from control, technology, finance and operations responsibilities without assuming that every firm uses the same front-office, middle-office and back-office labels. Operations is often the function that helps records, instructions, confirmations, settlements and exceptions move through controlled handoffs. It is a real finance career pathway, but it is not identical to advisory, research or trading.
The main investment banking team groups

items: Advisory and capital-raising teams may support defined corporate transactions, subject to the firm's permissions and applicable rules.
Markets teams may support activity in securities or other products; client, execution and control duties can differ by organisation.
Research teams prepare analysis under their own review and disclosure controls; their work is distinct from operational processing.
Risk, compliance, legal and control teams challenge, monitor or stop activity when a policy, risk or obligation requires it.
Finance and technology teams support reporting, valuation, systems, data and infrastructure that other teams depend on.
Operations teams coordinate records, confirmations, settlement, reconciliations, static data and exception management.

body.text: A simplified transaction lifecycle might begin with an authorised decision or execution, followed by capture of the terms, confirmation with relevant parties, preparation of settlement instructions, movement of cash or securities, reconciliation and exception closure. Different teams own different points in that sequence. An operations analyst should be able to say which record is being checked, what evidence is expected, what happens when values disagree and who can approve a correction. That is more useful than memorising a team chart.

Suppose a fictional markets team records a bond purchase with a settlement date of 12 October, while the custodian file shows 13 October. The operations analyst checks the trade reference, confirms whether an approved amendment exists, reviews the time zone and market calendar used by the system, and records the evidence. They do not decide that one date is correct because it looks more convenient. If the mismatch could affect a deadline, the analyst escalates it through the documented control route and records the owner and expected response.

items: Operations: reconciliation, process controls, data quality, deadline management and exception writing.
Risk and compliance: policy interpretation, evidence review, monitoring and escalation judgement.
Finance: accounting logic, reporting controls, variance analysis and clear documentation.
Technology and data: system thinking, requirements, data lineage and controlled change.
Client or market roles: product knowledge, communication and activity-specific rules.

body.text: How to evaluate a job description

Look for the actual daily work: the queue or portfolio, systems used, service-level expectations, reviewer model, shift pattern, required product knowledge and the decisions the role may make. Ask how quality is measured and what an analyst does when a break cannot be resolved. Treat salary, placement and employer claims as items to verify directly, not as a reason to infer that one title is better than another.
